Name: Ashli Woodgate
Description:
Ashli passed away in her home. She was studying computer science at UEA and was on a waiting list for a first appointment at a Gender Identity Clinic.

> Ashli Woodgate, 20, was found dead at a house on Crummock Road in Earlham, Norwich, on December 1 last year.
> 
> The inquest at Norfolk Coroners Court heard that Ashli, who was from Stockton-on-Tees in County Durham, had long struggled with depression and anxiety and had been self-medicating with alcohol and drugs since the age of 18-years-old.
>
> Ashli - who was born male but later identified as female - had been diagnosed with gender identity disorder in 2020 and was on a waiting list for treatment. Mother Amy Woodgate described Ashli - who was referred to with female pronouns during the hearing - as “a very bright individual” who moved to Norwich to study computer science at UEA.
> 
> The court heard Ashli, who also worked as a part-time bar attendant, met “like-minded people” in the trans community after moving to the city and began a relationship with a close friend.
> 
> Ms Woodgate said she last spoke to her child on November 24, when Ashli told her about a trip to Brighton.
> 
> However, over the following days, Ms Woodgate was unable to reach Ashli and she became increasingly worried. By November 30, Ashli’s phone was no longer ringing. A friend later called the ambulance service, and Ashli was found dead at home.
> 
> A statement from Penny Voyce, a fellow UEA student who had been in an on-off relationship with Ashli, said: “Ashli told me a few times that drugs were the only thing making her happy.”
> 
> The inquest heard Ashli had sought help from Change Grow Live, a service supporting people with alcohol and drug problems. Recording a conclusion of drug-related death, area coroner for Norfolk Yvonne Blake said: “I’m very sorry about your daughter. It’s a terrible thing to happen. You feel so helpless as parents to deal with this.”

Ashli was born in Stockton-on-Tees in County Durham.

Name: Mau Hijra
Description:
Mau passed away in suspicious circumstances. According to *JusticeMakers Bangladesh in France*, her death appears to be a premeditated act of murder disguised as natural causes.

The fact that her possessions were looted following her death supports this.

> Statement: JMBF Calls for Adequate Investigation into the Alleged Murder of Mau Hijra in Jessore
> 
> Paris, France; January 2, 2025: France-based human rights organization, JusticeMakers Bangladesh in France (JMBF), is deeply appalled and outraged by the suspicious and tragic death of Mau Hijra in Jessore, Bangladesh, which appears to be a premeditated act of murder disguised as a natural death on December 1, 2024.
> 
> JMBF believes that such abhorrent acts not only represent a blatant violation of human dignity but also highlight the rampant impunity and discrimination faced by marginalized communities, particularly the Hijra community in Bangladesh.
> 
> The organization asserts that the allegations against Mau Hijra's house owner, Fateh Begum, along with her associates—who are accused of orchestrating her death and looting her possessions—demand an immediate and uncompromising investigation.
> 
> Additionally, the Hijra community’s voice, as articulated by Bhavna Hijra, deserves urgent attention and support. No individual or community should endure such heinous acts of violence, neglect, and theft, especially in a society that claims to uphold justice and equality.
> 
> “The death of Mau Hijra and the looting of her belongings reflect a troubling pattern of systemic neglect and discrimination against the Hijra community in Bangladesh. We urge the Bangladeshi authorities to take swift and decisive action to ensure justice is served and to prevent such tragedies in the future,” said Robert Simon, Chief Adviser of JMBF and a French human rights activist.
> 
> “This incident is not an isolated one but a symptom of deeper societal injustices. We demand the immediate formation of an independent investigative body to uncover the truth and hold all those responsible accountable. The time for justice and reform is now,” added Advocate Shahanur Islam, Founder-President of JMBF and a Bangladeshi human rights lawyer.
> 
> JMBF calls upon the authorities in Bangladesh to take decisive action, including the immediate formation of an independent and impartial investigative body to uncover the truth behind Mau Hijra’s death. All individuals involved in this alleged murder and subsequent looting must be brought to justice without delay.
> 
> JMBF emphasizes that this incident reflects a broader pattern of systemic discrimination against the Hijra community in Bangladesh, underscoring the urgent need for reforms to safeguard their rights and ensure their protection under the law.
> 
> The organization demands that the Bangladeshi government reaffirm its commitment to the principles of equality and justice by taking concrete steps to protect all vulnerable communities, including decriminalizing homosexuality and enacting legal protections for the sexual minority LGBTQ community in Bangladesh as soon as possible.
> 
> JusticeMakers Bangladesh in France (JMBF) stands in solidarity with the Hijra community in their pursuit of justice for Mau Hijra. Together with human rights advocates around the world, we will not rest until truth and accountability are achieved in this case. Let this be a turning point in the fight against violence, discrimination, and systemic injustice in Bangladesh.

Name: Ra'lasia Wright
Description:
Ra'lasia's was found shot dead in a driveway after her friends and family located her via a cellphone location tracking app.

Authorities are still investigating her murder.

> MINNEAPOLIS — On Saturday night at 11:04 p.m., Camilla Lieng, one of Ra'Lasia Wright's best friends, received an iPhone SOS emergency text indicating that "Ra'Lasia called emergency services after the iPhone detected a crash." The message included a map with a location adjacent to Powderhorn Park in South Minneapolis. 
>
> Lieng wasn't able to reach Ra'Lasia and assumed there was no actual emergency.
>
> "I thought she was going to the club or something or something happened where she accidentally hit her SOS button because that does happen. I didn't get in contact with her and it was late at night, so I went to bed," Lieng said.
>
> The next morning, other friends and family hadn't heard from Wright either. 
>
> So they followed Wright's shared location on their phones — the same as the SOS message — and found her shot and killed. Wright's body was lying on a driveway between two houses. Both homeowners told KARE 11 News they didn't see or hear anything.
>
>" There are a lot of speculations... like, who were you with that night?" Lieng said.
>
> Several unanswered questions remain. Lieng said Wright had no connection to that neighborhood. There was no evidence of a car crash and no indication of how Wright got there.
>
> Wright was transgender and Camilla said she stood up for others in the community. She describes her friend as outgoing and protective — but also polarizing. 
>
> "She loved her friends she loved her family. She just wanted to make sure everyone was good. As long as you didn't mess with her, there were no issues," Lieng said. "Ra'Lasia did have some ongoing social media issues but that's just her. "
>
> Hoping that the killer is swiftly caught, Lieng said she will miss her friend.
>
> "She took me under her wing and brought me around her people and they showed me love and loved me and now I don't have anyone else to go anywhere with," Lieng said.

Friends say Ra'Lasia Wright was well-known in the Minneapolis club scene and had no connection to the neighborhood where her body was found.

Name: E. Nascimento de Lima
Description:
E. was killed by a client inside a residence. Her killer then attempted to dismember her.

> The Municipal Civil Guard (GCM) of Rio Verde arrested around 1 am this Monday (2) a man accused of stabbing [deadname] Nascimento de Lima, 34, to death inside a residence on Rua Otoni Carvalho, in the Jacutinga neighborhood, in Jataí. The information is from the Rota Policial Notícias profile.
> 
> The GCM agents were informed by a team from the Fire Department (CBMGO), which was already on site, that there was a naked and injured man inside the residence and that he was refusing help.
> 
> The perpetrator, aged 37, was approached by the GCMs and reported that he had hired [deadname], a [trans woman], to deliver drugs to his home and invited the victim to use the drugs together.
> 
> According to him, the two had a disagreement over the price charged for the drug, they got into a physical fight and the victim was stabbed in the neck, dying at the scene.
> 
> The residence showed signs of extreme violence, with a large amount of blood in the rooms. The GCM found [deadname's] body in the external area of the house. The accused even tried to dismember the victim before the police arrived.
> 
> The body was sent to the Legal Medical Institute (IML)
> 
> The body will be buried this afternoon in Jataí. The family, who lives in another city, preferred not to hold a wake.

In October 2025 Anderson Dias Nogueira was sentenced 30 years in prison for aggravated femicide and an additional year for destruction and concealment of a body.

Alana was shot dead while in a restaurant/bar with friends. Earlier in the year she had become the first trans woman to run for a seat on her local city council.

> 
> Alana was the first trans woman to run for a seat on the city council. A candidate for the Avante party in the 2024 elections, she received 52 votes but was not elected. She was known for her charisma, humility and for fighting for her ideals.
> 
> A friend who witnessed the crime said in an interview with  Itatiaia  that Alana was “a very good person at heart, energetic and fearless”. He highlighted her determination to occupy spaces of representation in local politics.
> 
> Authorities have not yet released details about the motives behind the crime, which is still being investigated by the Civil Police. Alana's death has caused consternation and sparked discussions about the challenges faced by the LGBTQIA+ population in their search for representation and respect.

Name: Thitikarn Dulikanon ("Dr Sammy")

>

>

Name: Roy Mora
Description:
Roy died by suicide. The Roy Mora Memorial Scholarship  - available to all LGBTQIA+ high school students in Mendocino County - was established in his honour.

> FORT BRAGG, CA., 12/23/24 — A body found under Noyo River Bridge Monday morning was wearing jewelry that belonged to missing teen Roy Mora, a press release from the Fort Bragg Police Department said. Mora’s mother identified the necklace, the press release said.
>
> Police said the body was not identifiable otherwise. An unidentified person found the body just after 8 a.m. Monday morning and called dispatch. Although officers who arrived could not identify the body, they noted the person was wearing the same clothes Mora was wearing when he disappeared. The area around the bridge had been searched dozens of times by law enforcement and volunteers.
>
> A search has been going on for more than two weeks after Mora, 15, disappeared following the Dec 7 Lighted Truck Parade in downtown Fort Bragg. A barista at the Mendocino Cookie Company identified Mora’s phone when a man living nearby in his car turned it into the coffee shop. She had seen it on the brochures around town and called the police.
>
> Police used that evidence, cell phone location and other data to triangulate Mora’s whereabouts. They tracked him entering Noyo Bridge shortly after the parade. His phone was found on the sidewalk of the bridge, but no cameras showed him leaving, nor did police find evidence that cars slowed down on the bridge.

Name: Neuritânia Pacheco
Description:
Neuritânia's body was found on a football field after she had left her home to go on a date. She was a civil servant who worked at Sobradinho City Hall.

> A 48-year-old trans woman was found dead in the city of Sobradinho, in northern Bahia. According to information given to g1 on Monday (16), the victim's body had signs of violence and there is a suspicion that she was stoned.
> 
> The crime took place on Saturday (14), near a soccer field in Vila São Francisco. According to family members, Neuritânia Pacheco had left home for a date. However, it is not yet known whether this was related to the crime.
> 
> The body of the victim, who was a civil servant at the Sobradinho City Hall, was sent to the Technical Police Department (DPT) in the region. The wake and burial took place on Sunday (15), at the city cemetery, according to information provided by TV São Francisco, an affiliate of Rede Bahia in the region.
> 
> The perpetrator and motive for the murder are being investigated by the Sobradinho Territorial Police Station, where the case was registered. The police are awaiting the expert report from the DPT. As of Monday, no one had been arrested.
> 
> On social media, the mayor of Sobradinho, Cleyvinho Sampaio (PSD), shared a note of condolence for Neuritânia's death, expressing solidarity with the employee's family and friends. She worked as a general services assistant at the Municipal Department of Tourism, Culture and Sports.
> 
> "The Mayor of Sobradinho, Cleyvinho Sampaio, deeply regrets the tragic death of civil servant Neuritânia Pacheco. Neuritânia stood out for her friendliness and charisma with the public and coworkers and leaves a legacy of dedication and services provided to the community.
> 
> The mayor also emphasizes that he has already requested all efforts and agility from the police authorities in the investigation of this barbaric crime. To the family and friends of our friend Neuritânia, our solidarity and strength in this moment of extreme pain."

In January 2025 two teenage suspects were arrested on charges similar to qualified homicide.

Description:
Z died by suicide. They were a writer whose work included the upcoming Game of Thrones spinoff series "Knight of the Seven Kingdoms".

> Television writer Aziza "Z" Barnes, whose work included an upcoming Game of Thrones spinoff series, has passed away. Barnes was just 32 years old.
> 
> Per Deadline, Barnes died by suicide on Sunday, Dec. 15, with their family confirming the news through a rep. There were no additional details shared about the circumstances of Barnes' death, though the family shared a statement to announce the news while expressing their sorrow over the loss..
> 
> “With heavy hearts, we regret to inform you of the passing of an undeniable and beloved artist, child, sibling, and friend Aziza ‘Z’ Barnes,” the statement reads. “Z has touched and inspired countless individuals both in their community and industry and will be deeply missed and endlessly loved by all who were fortunate to have experienced their presence and work. An incomparable talent, we look for understanding in Z’s words, and wish comfort and understanding as we grieve this loss.”
> 
> Barnes earned a BFA from New York University and attended the University of Mississippi to pursue an MFA. They had also served as a member of the award-winning NYU Poetry Slam team. Barnes won an Exploding Pinecone Prize from Button Poetry as the author of the 2013 chapbook me Aunt Jemima and the nailgun, and their poetry collection, i be but i ain't, won a Pamet River Prize from YesYes Books. They also wrote the acclaimed stage show BLKS.
> 
> Barnes also pursued work as a TV writer, working on shows like FX's Snowfall, Netflix's Teenage Bounty Hunters, and Max's Rap Sh!t. Additionally, Barnes worked as a writer on HBO's upcoming Game of Thrones spinoff series, titled A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms; the show is set to be released on HBO in 2025.
> 
> Immediate details were not made available about Barnes' survivors.
> 
> Source: Deadline
> 
> If you or someone you know is thinking about suicide, emotional support is offered 24/7 through the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, available by texting or calling 988. A chat option is also available on the official website.

Name: Cam Thompson
Description:
Cam's body was found in a yard near her home. A male suspect was arrested and charged as an adult in her murder.

The suspect was booked into the Tuscaloosa County Jail.

> TUSCALOOSA, Ala. (WIAT) — A Tuscaloosa family struggles to come to grips with the loss of their loved one, 18-year-old [deadname] Thompson who went by Cam.
>
> On Thursday afternoon, CBS 42 News spoke the victim’s aunt in Tuscaloosa.
>
> “We’re just devastated, like we’re still in shock,” said Tara Maneice. “We cannot believe that this happened you know so quickly, out of nowhere.”
>
> According to the Tuscaloosa County Violent Crimes Unit, Thompson, who identified as a woman, died after being shot in the 600 block of East 35th Avenue shortly after midnight on Monday. Capt. Jack Kennedy said a minor has been arrested and charged as an adult in her murder. He has been booked into the Tuscaloosa County Jail.
>
> We asked Maneice to describe her niece:
>
> “A beautiful smile, very contagious smile,” she noted, “loved fashion and the beauty industry.”
>
> Thompson, who was a transgender woman, had just completed Job Corps training and had a bright future ahead of her.
>
> “All these plans she had, she was getting ready to try to go to college, buy a new car, that they have been just wiped away in the blink of an eye, a senseless act,” Maneice added.
>
> The Tuscaloosa County Violent Crimes Unit was called to investigate Thompson’s shooting after her body was discovered near the street in a yard around 1 p.m. on Monday.
>
> Captain Kennedy said the motive appears to be related to comments that Thompson posted on social media regarding the suspect’s sexual orientation.
>
> “They were having a personal argument between each other, knew each other, and that seems to be the impetus behind this assault and murder.”
>
> Maneice said the mother believes this was a hate crime based on her daughter’s gender identity. Alabama’s hate law only pertains to crimes motivated by victim’s race, color, religion, national origin, ethnicity, or physical or mental disability.

Name: Mayla Gomes
Description:
Mayla was a hairdresser. Her body was found in woodland two days after she had gone missing from her home.

> Mayla Gomes, a trans woman who worked as a hairdresser and who had been missing since the night of last Saturday (14) was found dead on Monday (16), in Novo Progresso, in the southwest of Pará. Friends reported that, when looking for her at her residence, they found the mattress with blood stains, which raised concerns.  
> 
> Preliminary information indicates that Mayla had taken a young man home before disappearing without leaving any clues. The case was reported to the police, who began searching the area. Last Monday (16), Mayla's body was found in a wooded area in the Jardim Santarém neighborhood. The Forensic Medical Institute (IML) was called and removed the body, which showed clear signs of violence, especially on the arms and legs.  
> 
> To date, the case remains a mystery. Investigations will need to clarify whether the crime was motivated by passion or whether it was a hate crime related to the victim's gender identity.  
> 
> In a statement, the Civil Police reported that teams from the Novo Progresso police station are working to identify and arrest those involved. The case, initially treated as a robbery with concealment of a corpse, is still under investigation. Expert reports have been requested, and witnesses should be heard in the coming days to assist in the progress of the investigation.

Name: Bianca Castyel ("Bia")
Description:
Bianca was a hairdresser. Her killer - a young man who according to police exhibited psychopathic tendencies - was arrested after her murdered body was found in her bed.

> The Civil Police of Água Boa (730 km from Cuiabá) complied, on the afternoon of this Sunday (22), with the judicial orders to investigate the murder of the young trans woman, Bianca Castyel, 20 years old, who was executed with 22 stab wounds on the afternoon of last Thursday (19).
>
A 17-year-old teenager was identified as the author of the brutal murder and had an arrest and internment order fulfilled by the PJC. Investigations revealed that on the night of the events the young man and the victim, who was a hairdresser, met and had sexual relations. It was also found that they had a previous relationship, however, possibly after the sexual act the suspect executed the victim with stab wounds and strangulation.
> 
> Delegate Matheus Soares Augusto, responsible for the case, highlighted the criminal profile of the suspect who presents psychopathic tendencies that are revealed by the coldness of executing the victim after the intimate act, indicating that it was something previously planned, as well as the fact that the teenager did not show remorse for what happened and the next day returned to his normal routine and went on a vacation with his family.
> 
> The victim's cell phone and the knife used in the crime were discarded by the teenager to hinder the investigation. The name of the operation "Rest in Peace" is a tribute to the life of the victim who was brutally executed, said the police chief.
> 
> Since the beginning of the investigation, the detective had been working with the possibility that the killer was someone close to the victim, as the property showed no signs of a break-in and the door was just opened.

Name: Meka Shabazz
Description:
Meka died by suicide. She was an accomplished dancer, community activist, teacher, and mentor who taught Afro Caribbean dance and GED courses and actively mentored young people.

> In December, my friend Meka Shabazz died after [suicide method redacted].
> 
> Rates of suicide are disproportionately high for transgender people. According to a study published by the National Institutes of Health, "41% of the transgender persons in the United States attempt for suicide at least once in their life."
> 
> High rates of suicidality are not a symptom of being transgender. Rather, it is the difficulty of living in a threatening world that becomes too much weight to carry.
> 
> I have spent hours on the phone crying with people who loved her, danced with her and worked for justice with her.
> 
> She could be strong-willed and sometimes drive us crazy. But as we say at the United Methodist Church for All People, “No matter who you are or what you have done, you are a beloved child of God.”
> 
> Meka’s belovedness was wiped out.
> 
> **Our hatred killed her.**

> This hatred must stop.
> 
> I made an Instagram video making the same point — that we have to say "enough" to the hatred and division that kills people.
> 
> In response, I received a litany of hateful messages saying "enough" of people like me, calling transgender people sick and asking, “So what?” that Meka died.
> 
> Hatred kills.
> 
> Hatred results in the death of people like Meka.
> 
> Hatred tears up the person who is doing the hating.
> 
> Love can save others.
>
> Christmas marked the incarnation of God’s love into the world in Jesus the Christ.
> 
> I pray that this love will be born anew and that we can learn to recognize the belovedness of all people.
> 
> Hatred killed my friend. Enough.
> 
> It is time to come out of this darkness. Let us learn the truth that when we love instead of hate, we don’t only save the other, we save ourselves.  
> 
> Meka Shabazz's memorial service will take place at 1:30 p.m. Jan. 4 at the United Methodist Church for All People, 946 Parsons Ave. All are welcome to come and celebrate this beautiful life.
> 
> Rev. Dr. Joelle Henneman is pastor of United Methodist Church for All People. 


In [her blog](https://historianspeaks.org/blog/f/living-one-dance-at-a-time--meka-shabazz
) Meka wrote the following, which I think says a lot about her character:

> "My message to all people going through a difficult time is to put on your big girl pants and humble yourself. At the peak of my success everything I worked so hard for was lost, but I persevered.
>
> "To the LGBTQA community not everyone will be accepting of who you are. They may try to break you and harass you emotionally. Maintain yourself by keeping yourself polished. When mistreated as a result of gender discrimination, you must continue to believe in yourself. You must be persistent."

Name: Mirella Albuquerque
Description:
Mirella was stabbed in the drug rehab centre where she was undertaking vocational training courses as a step towards rebuilding her life.

> A trans woman was stabbed to death in a shelter in Cabo de Santo Agostinho, in Greater Recife, this Wednesday (25). The suspect of the crime, who was also hospitalized in the unit, managed to escape before the police arrived. 
> 
> The victim was identified as Mirella Albuquerque, 21 years old. She had been hospitalized for four months in the social assistance center linked to the Atitude program, aimed at treating drug users, under the responsibility of the state government. 
> 
> Few details were released about the crime. In a statement, the State Secretariat for Social Assistance, Fight Against Hunger and Drug Policies said only that it had called SAMU and the police to provide assistance to the woman. "The victim was pronounced dead at the scene and the suspect, also taken into care at the center, threatened the team and managed to escape before the police forces arrived," the text said.
> 
> The state department did not say whether the trans woman and the suspect had any relationship. The Civil Police of Pernambuco was asked whether the case is being treated as a femicide, but did not respond.
> 
> On the morning of this Thursday (26), family members were at the Institute of Legal Medicine (IML), in the Santo Amaro neighborhood, central area of Recife, to release the body. 
> 
> They told the TV Jornal team that Mirella had little contact with her family in recent months because of her addiction treatment. She only left the unit once or twice a month, always accompanied by a social worker. During this time, she began vocational training courses, such as nursing technician, to try to change her life. 
> 
> The State Secretariat for Social Assistance, Combating Hunger and Drug Policies stated that it "deeply regrets what happened and clarifies that it is providing support to the host family, as well as the team that continues to provide support to the people served at the unit. "

Mirella's killer was arrested in February 2025. Reportedly he killed her because she told others of their relationship.

Name: Micaela Arévalo
Description:
Micaela died after being stabbed in the neck and chest with the edge of a broken bottle by a teenage boy. A 15 year-old was subsequently arrested.

> A tragic episode shook the southern area of Greater Buenos Aires on Sunday night, when a trans woman was [stabbed in the neck] in a street fight. The authorities arrested a 15-year-old teenager, who is presumed to have used the edge of a vodka bottle to carry out the attack. The judicial authorities rule out robbery as a motive for the murder and are working to clarify the causes of the dispute.
> 
> The violent incident occurred at the intersection of Avenida Mozart and Calle Guido. Judicial spokesmen reported that the victim and the minor involved engaged in an altercation, during which the young man attacked the trans woman and subsequently fled the scene. Minutes later, officers from the Patrol Command went to the scene after receiving a call to 911 alerting them about the fight.
> 
> Upon arrival, the officers found the victim's body lying on the sidewalk, surrounded by blood stains. Forensic experts confirmed that the woman had a deep wound in the neck, as well as cuts in the thoracic area. At the scene, remains of a vodka bottle were found that had been used as a weapon.
> 
> Based on images obtained from security cameras in the area, investigators were able to identify and arrest the suspect at the corner of calles Moreno and Rivadavia, a well-known predestrianised commercial area. According to reports, the young man arrested is currently homeless. By legal provision, his identity has not been disclosed.
> 
> Although the identity of the victim and the origin of the conflict are unknown, the authorities believe that the teenager knew the trans woman. The Juvenile Criminal Responsibility Prosecutor's Office No. 1 of the jurisdiction is involved in the case, which has been preliminarily classified as "Homicide."
> 
> The case has caused consternation and reflection in the community due to the violence involved and the young age of the alleged aggressor. Investigations are continuing to determine the exact circumstances of the incident and the possible background between the parties involved.

Name: Jonny Adamow
Description:
Jonny died after being caught in crossfire on New Year's Eve. They were nonbinary, gender nonconforming, and heavily involved in the Seattle drag and renaissance faire communities.

> Jonathan “Jonny” Adamow, 29, was a beautiful person who loved all living beings. Jonny’s life was tragically taken on the morning of December 31st, 2024, on the streets of Seattle, Washington.
> 
> Jonny was born in Manhattan on July 6th, 1995, raised in Flushing, Queens, and moved to Stony Point, where [they] attended North Rockland High School. As a lover of the arts, Jonny acted in both their school’s drama club and off-Broadway theater. [They were] a talented percussionist, performing in his high school marching band. Always drawing and equipped with a sketchbook, Jonny attended Rockland Community College for fine arts.
> 
> Active and creative, Jonny enjoyed rollerblading, exploring nature, and creating music. As an avid artist, [they] had a great ability to spread light and kindness to everyone [they] met all over the world. Jonny will be remembered for their authenticity, compassion, love, and radiant energy, calling many places in the world their home. [They] spread light and joy everywhere [they] went and positively impacted all who crossed their path.
> 
> Jonny was a very loved member of the Renaissance Faire community, of which they were a part of since 2010. As a humanitarian, Jonny also served as a team leader for natural disaster relief and wanted the best for everyone. [They were] also a valued team leader of various trail crews throughout America, working in conservation and habitat restoration. [They] respected and adored the natural world and worked to preserve it.

A vigil was held for Jonny on the evening Friday 10th January.
